name: Pavement
label: Matador
lede: Stephen Malkmus and Scott Kannberg cut a first EP in a Stockton drummer's house, took mud and rocks at Lollapalooza, hung handcuffs on a mic stand at Brixton, and came back to find a 1999 B-side had become their biggest song.

eras.title: A studio project in Stockton
eras.text: Pavement started as a studio project, not a band: Stephen Malkmus and Scott Kannberg, calling themselves S.M. and Spiral Stairs, recording in a Stockton, California house studio owned by a drummer twenty years older than them. The early singles sounded like static with a songwriter hiding inside.

years.h: Malkmus and Kannberg book themselves as S.M. and Spiral Stairs
years.p: [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] and [[Scott Kannberg|632a2bce-6f80-458b-a375-649ddffb03e0]] start Pavement in Stockton, California, as a recording project with no band attached.

years.big: "this Malkmus idiot is a complete songwriting genius"
years.h: Gary Young sizes up the kid he is recording
years.p: [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]], a local hippie drummer, said it of Stephen Malkmus. The debut EP, Slay Tracks: 1933–1969, is cut at Young's home studio, Louder Than You Think, and he ends up playing on it and joining.
years.xp:
Young's line, as Wikipedia prints it, is the one above. Malkmus was the "idiot" he meant.

Jason Turner briefly replaced Young in 1989 and left over clashes with Malkmus, who later called him "very competitive." Young was reinstated after one tour and a few sessions.

years.h: Pavement's live debut goes out over college radio
years.p: The college station KDVS-FM in Davis, California, carries the first Pavement performance live.

years.h: Drag City puts out Demolition Plot J-7
years.p: Chicago's Drag City releases the second Pavement EP. A guitarist, Rob Chamberlin, passes through the line-up the same year.

years.h: Nastanovich and Ibold turn Pavement into a live band
years.p: Malkmus's New York roommate [[Bob Nastanovich|4bcaf5b5-89a5-4712-8a11-6d60dd0904f5]] joins on percussion and shouting, and [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]] takes bass.

years.h: Perfect Sound Forever, EP number three
years.p: Recorded at Gary Young's studio, like the first two.

eras.title: Gary Young is the show, until he can't be
eras.text: Slanted and Enchanted circulated on tape before Matador released it. Onstage, drummer Gary Young was the show, until his drinking made the show impossible.

years.h: Slanted and Enchanted circulates on tape before Matador releases it
years.p: Rolling Stone later puts the debut on its 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
years.xp: Recorded at Young's Louder Than You Think, it became one of the most cited indie rock albums of the 1990s: fractured songs, heavy distortion and stream-of-consciousness words over a lo-fi hiss.

years.cap: Pavement with drummer Gary Young, c. 1992
years.h: Gary Young hands cabbage and mashed potatoes to fans at the door
years.p: On the Slanted and Enchanted tour the drummer also does handstands, runs around mid-set and falls off his stool drunk.
years.xp: Malkmus later said the band knew Young was a flaky hippie, but hadn't known how bad his drinking problem was.

years.h: Three bandmates stay silent while Nastanovich confronts Gary Young
years.p: At a Copenhagen hotel after the 1993 tour of Australia, Japan and Europe, Nastanovich, Young's best friend in the band, argues with him. Malkmus, Kannberg and Ibold say nothing, and [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]] agrees to leave.
years.xp: Young stayed gone until the 2010 reunion, when he came back for an encore in Stockton.

years.h: Steve West's first show is a Drag City festival in Chicago
years.p: [[Steve West|c4705a05-ffdd-4441-a852-0aeb94de4c9b]] takes over the drums.

years.h: A love letter to R.E.M. lands on the No Alternative benefit album
years.p: Unseen Power of the Picket Fence appears on the Red Hot Organization's AIDS-benefit compilation as a song about [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]].

eras.title: The band that ruined Lollapalooza
eras.text: Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain put Pavement on MTV and late-night TV, and one song on it picked a fight with a headliner. A year later the band made its most sprawling record and got mud thrown at it.

years.h: Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain puts Pavement on MTV
years.p: Cut Your Hair gets MTV and alternative radio play, and the band lands a spot on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno.

years.h: Billy Corgan threatens to pull the Pumpkins over a Pavement song
years.p: Range Life takes shots at [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]] and [[Stone Temple Pilots|8c32bb01-58a3-453b-8050-8c0620edb0e5]]. [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]] says the Pumpkins won't headline Lollapalooza 1994 if Pavement plays.
years.xp:
Malkmus said the song was light-hearted and sung from the view of an aging hippie character. Corgan did not take it that way, and the two traded press barbs for years.

The Pumpkins headlined; Pavement did not play the 1994 tour. They got their turn the next summer.

years.h: Wowee Zowee follows a hit with 18 tracks of punk, country and ballads
years.p: The follow-up to the MTV record sprawls. Malkmus later said his picks for singles sounded like hits to him.
years.xp: His explanation: "I was smoking a lot of grass back then but to me they sounded like hits."

years.h: Lollapalooza crowds throw mud and rocks, and Pavement walks off
years.p: On the 1995 Lollapalooza tour the band skips setlists for loose, drug- and drink-fueled jams.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the sets incoherent, and many in the crowd answered with hostility. The band left the stage and gave itself a new title: The Band That Ruined Lollapalooza.

eras.title: The band ends without saying so
eras.text: Brighten the Corners came out tidy. Then Terror Twilight brought in Radiohead's producer, the sessions stalled over Scrabble, and Pavement finished at Brixton without anyone saying the word.

years.h: Mitch Easter produces Brighten the Corners
years.p: He worked on R.E.M.'s early records. The songs run shorter and straighter, with Stereo and Shady Lane as the singles.

years.h: Sessions stall over Scrabble, then Nigel Godrich takes over
years.p: At Jackpot! in Portland the band plays Scrabble instead of recording. [[Nigel Godrich|52de022d-5401-427f-8301-ff1b8be11a7a]] moves Terror Twilight to Sonic Youth's Manhattan studio, then to RPM near Washington Square Park.
years.xp:
Godrich wanted a record that would "stand up straighter" for listeners turned off by the sloppiness of other Pavement albums, and he asked for more takes than the band was used to giving.

Nastanovich said Godrich only connected with Malkmus and still didn't know the others' names after several days. Matador calls the album "a departure from Pavement's established operating methods."

years.h: After Coachella, Malkmus tells the band he's done
years.p: After Pavement's set at the 1999 Coachella Festival, [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] tells his bandmates he doesn't want to continue.

years.big: "These symbolize what it's like being in a band all these years."
years.h: Pavement's last show hangs handcuffs on the mic stand
years.p: [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] says it to the crowd at Brixton Academy in London. Nobody announces a breakup.
years.xp: Nastanovich, asked about the night later, said "there was too much exhaustion for heavy emotion."

years.h: The website tells Steve West his band is over
years.p: Malkmus phones Kannberg to say they are no longer a band and tells him to update the website. West says nobody ever called him; he found out online.

eras.title: One more lap, and a bad night in Las Vegas
eras.text: With Malkmus and Kannberg off in Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks and Preston School of Industry, Pavement became a DVD, a biography and a question. In 2010 they answered with a world tour, a hometown show and a bad night at the Palms.

years.h: Lance Bangs puts the Pavement videos on two DVDs
years.p: Lance Bangs's Slow Century is a two-DVD documentary set with the band's music videos and concert footage going back to 1989.

years.h: Central Park tickets sell out in two minutes
years.p: Brooklyn Vegan breaks the news of Central Park shows, the band confirms on September 17 and 18, and three more shows get added.
years.xp: The band said the Central Park run might only be a one-off, not the start of a reunion.

years.cap: Pavement at the Mann Center, Philadelphia, September 17, 2010
years.h: Auckland hosts Pavement's first show in over ten years
years.p: It starts a year-long world tour.

years.h: Pavement finally plays Stockton, and Gary Young comes out for the encore
years.p: At the Bob Hope Theatre, [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]] plays three songs from Slanted and Enchanted.

years.h: Kannberg kicks his monitor, then smashes his guitar, in Las Vegas
years.p: At Matador's 21st-birthday weekend at the Palms Casino, [[Scott Kannberg|632a2bce-6f80-458b-a375-649ddffb03e0]] kicks the monitor and puts the guitar through his amp. NME notes an icy atmosphere onstage.
years.xp: Wikipedia says he was frustrated by inadequate stage monitoring.

eras.title: A B-side goes viral
eras.text: Pavement came back as a band whose old fans had kids and whose new fans found them on TikTok. The second reunion lost Gary Young, got a musical and a film, and produced a new song.

years.h: Primavera Sound books Pavement for 2020
years.p: Two sets are announced; the pandemic pushes them to 2022.

years.h: Twenty years late, Harness Your Hopes finds TikTok
years.p: The 1999 B-side from the Spit on a Stranger EP spreads on TikTok and becomes Pavement's most-streamed song.

years.cap: Pavement at The Masonic, San Francisco, c. 2022
years.h: The Fonda Theatre sells out for Pavement's return
years.p: [[Rebecca Cole|9a8de0df-12bf-41ed-8752-46cfcec70923]] of [[The Minders|a0cf076f-2fa8-476a-84e2-6d9980c0deb9]] and [[Wild Flag|4473e47b-81bb-47af-8cb0-1cad6f68d8bc]] joins on keyboards. Tours of North America and Europe follow.

years.h: A Pavement musical opens off-Broadway
years.p: Slanted! Enchanted! A Pavement Musical opens in New York, built from Pavement songs around a Malkmus-like hero.

years.h: Louder Than You Think brings Gary Young to SXSW
years.p: The documentary on Pavement's first drummer premieres five months before he dies.

years.h: Gary Young, the first drummer, dies at 70
years.p: [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]] owned the Stockton studio where Pavement made its first records.

years.h: Pavement closes the year at The National's Homecoming in Cincinnati
years.p: Billed as the last show for a while, at Smale Park during [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]]'s festival.

years.cap: Pavement at Sony Hall, New York, October 2024
years.h: A one-off at Sony Hall for the Pavements premiere
years.p: The film about the band opens the New York Film Festival run. Nastanovich calls the show the last one for a long time.

years.h: A new Pavement song is coming, 25 years on
years.p: Kannberg says the Pavements soundtrack will carry it, the first new Pavement song in more than twenty-five years.

years.h: A short 2026 run opens in Oakland and ends in Atlanta
years.p: It starts July 19 at Mosswood Meltdown and finishes September 19 at Shaky Knees.
